body.statement: For every sequence in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\), the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the law of \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\) and the law of \(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)}\) tends to zero whenever criterion ties with positive Gaussian probability occur only between coordinates whose \(d_n\)-distance tends to zero. Consequently the same representation holds for fixed, vanishing, and exact leading-MSE gaps; the selector is an oracle Gaussian coordinate when the minimum gap diverges relative to the quadratic criterion noise, and it is a correlated Gaussian-quadratic argmin coordinate at a local or exact gap.
body.justification: The quadratic argmin law is the correct boundary distribution because Yang's bias estimate is squared at the same scale at which local bias is learned.
body.gap: Claeskens and Hjort and Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess derive focused-selection laws for fixed model lists; neither result includes an estimated individual influence ranking and its full nested prefix path.
body.consumer: A hybrid-trial analyst can simulate the correct selected-estimator law instead of applying a single-prefix Wald approximation after an unstable MSE comparison.
